Full agreement. Both evaluations strongly support the Myocd epistasis analysis (C75-C79, C113-C114) showing SMC loss is insufficient for cyst formation. OpenEval highlights this as 'critical genetic evidence'; peer reviewers implicitly accept it as supporting non-canonical BMP signaling.

Agreement on elastin findings (C54-C57). OpenEval supports the data with both in vivo and in vitro evidence; peer reviewers accept these mechanistic details without challenge as part of the compelling evidence for mesenchymal BMP signaling disruption.

Agreement on Smad-independent mechanism (C11, C58-C64). OpenEval provides detailed support noting the differential phenotype as critical evidence; peer reviewer explicitly highlights this finding as 'interesting' and accepts the role for non-canonical BMP signaling.

Agreement on epithelial perturbations (C9, C80-C84). OpenEval supports findings with convergent protein and mRNA data; peer reviewer explicitly notes the Sox2-Sox9 changes as accepted evidence of proximal-distal patterning defects.

Agreement on BMP ligand upregulation and feedback (C10, C86-C87, C125). OpenEval supports the inverse relationship between receptor and ligand expression; peer reviewer accepts these findings as part of the epithelial perturbation mechanism, though both note C125 is inferential.

Partial overlap on p38 mechanism (C69-C70). OpenEval supports in vitro BMP4 effects on SMC genes via p38 but notes these are cell culture findings. Peer reviewer views p38 data as suggestive but not conclusive, requiring additional validation.

Agreement on SMC heterogeneity (C71-C72). OpenEval supports the FACS-based differential response analysis as 'elegant' evidence for cell-type-specific effects; peer reviewers accept these in vitro findings without challenge.

Agreement on vascular specificity (C52-C53, C110). OpenEval supports negative findings for vascular SMCs and other ECM components as important specificity controls; peer reviewer notes acceptance that vascular structures were unaffected.

Partial agreement with reservations. Both address human CPAM relevance (C31, C91-C92, C119).
